steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Baryshnya Trepleva, it is quite clear to all present that Anna Morozova usurped your authority that night.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I am curious, however, as to why you did not choose to leave the Assembly, like other students did.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: That's because—

steps.name: Duke Treplev
steps.text: Your Honor, I believe the hearing should focus on specific events.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...The atmosphere at the time had compromised my reason.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: In that case, you must explain why you split from Anna's group, and how they kidnapped and coerced you.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...Yes, Your Honor.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Virtually everyone stayed at the theater that night, helping those who were injured, and thinking of ways to find out about those who were arrested.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But the situation changed the following day—

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: ...Alright, Olga, I applied what medicine I could find.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: It may not look good, but bear with me, it'll help you heal.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: You're on duty today? Where's Lada?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: You went to bed early last night. Natalya showed up later, along with a Vulpo I didn't know. They took Lada away after talking to Anna's group for a while.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Where's everyone else? The theater's all empty.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: I'm not sure, but I think Anna assigned missions.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: ...Our priority is to figure out where the students are being held captive.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Start with this list and talk to their parents, it may help us find a way.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I'll talk to my family contacts. Let me know if you have a lead; I'll verify it.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Take care, Anna.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Hm? What are you two doing here?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Olga was sleeping by the stage last night. I saw her wake up when I came to the theater in the morning, so I reapplied her medicine.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: ...Very good.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sergo, help me move Olga to the rehearsal studio on the third floor. She needs rest.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Perhaps I should go home, Anna.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'm good enough to walk now. I can't promise my father can help get people off, but at least I can ask where they're being held.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Don't worry, I already have a lead on where they're held.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: As for you, you should stay put and focus on recuperating. People will talk if you go home like this.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: There are other injured students staying behind to receive treatment. I'm having someone deliver their letters to their families.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: I'll get the stretcher, Olga.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: They moved me into a room, claiming to be protecting me.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But I soon realized that their 'protection' involved students standing at my door around the clock in shifts with fireman's axes in hand.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: When I tried to talk to them, I was told that they were under orders not to interact with me... so I gave up on writing to my father, because there was no way they would help me send it.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: So you realized you were being held captive by Anna Morozova?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Do you know her motivation to do such a thing?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: My guess is that I expressed reluctance when she hinted at exploiting the nobility the previous night.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Do you think it explains the Ursus Student Self-Government Group's hostility towards the aristocracy? It would be consistent with Sonya Mykhailivna colluding with the Unbound.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I wasn't the only one she imprisoned. Anyone who wasn't sufficiently firm in resolve, whom she deemed an information risk as well as... nobles who had value to her, were all treated the same way.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Did you have any opportunity to communicate with the outside or leave the room?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Very little, except for Sergo, who quietly told me what the students were doing when he was on duty, even telling me—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: ...Are you sure about this?

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: Absolutely! My mother has been running a garment factory in Grypherburg for more than a decade. You can trust us on this.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: But she said that approximately nine hundred winter army uniforms were being transported to the quarantine zone, while Natalya's observations yesterday indicates that there are no more than five hundred combatants there.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: If both of you are right, then there can only be one explanation—someone is sending reinforcements into the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: Sonya just said they couldn't deal with heavy weapons, and now reinforcements are being sent? What do we do, Anna?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Will your mother be at the factory these couple of days?

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: Yes, why?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I will speak to my police contacts, get a few uniforms, put some tall boys in them, and go to your mother's factory disguised as the gendarmes auditing the books.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Tell your mother that you don't have class for a few days, so you're helping out at the factory. Put in a word for us if your mother gets suspicious, tell her letting the cops see the books won't do any harm.

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: No hesitation. Our friends are in graver danger with every passing second. Trust my judgment, if you want to save them.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The source of this order is the breakthrough that we've been waiting for.

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: But impersonating the cops... that's way too hard.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: We haven't been in contact with our comms girl Botani since the ball, but the equipment that she left behind still works.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Bring the equipment and follow my orders. My friend who has police connections will be there to help...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sergo, are you there?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You're the tallest, you'll be the first to try the uniforms.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Me? But I get all red in the face whenever I go onstage in drama club. No way I could—

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: ...Play a cop.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Wow, my whole face is covered up...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Stop talking to yourself, Sergo. Watch the office door and don't let anyone come in.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Gotcha, Anna.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Do not respond verbally.
He nods reflexively, his throat moving up and down underneath his mask. He has had to swallow three times in the span of a single minute.
Anna's friend still has her head buried in the pile of documents on the office desk. Everything is going smoother than he expected, except for the part where he actually finds the answer.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Why is it taking so long—
What do you mean, taking so long...?
Wait, who are you? I thought we were supposed to be checking the books today—Unit 2.
Sergo turns around to find an authentic, non-impostor Ursine policeman staring at him perplexedly, or so he infers through the policeman's goggles.
He covers his mouth by reflex, although his counterpart would never have detected his anxiety if he did not do so.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: What's your district and unit? Did the new superintendent mix up the orders again?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Uh, uh, uh—

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Are you not feeling well? There's no fireplace or heating here. Why are you sweating like that...?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Slap him, Sergo.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Do it. My friend's coming your way.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Slap him, then yell at the top of your lungs, 'Do not delay the daughter of Lord Yaroslav!'

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: ...Do not delay the daughter of Lord Yaroslav!
He slaps the man with all his strength, and has to stop himself from crying out at the pain of his stinging palm.
The man stands where he is, reaching up to touch where he was slapped.

steps.name: Anna's Friend
steps.text: I apologize. The superintendent made a last-minute change, and the news apparently didn't reach you.

steps.name: Anna's Friend
steps.text: This man is my bodyguard, whom my family arranged to go into the service with me, for father was uneasy about me being alone.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: ...So it's like that again?

steps.name: Anna's Friend
steps.text: Yes, like that.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Command knew this factory's books were off, so they left it to some noble kid to reap the fruits.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: I've been in the force for three years, and it's the same every year. Every time there's a new superintendent, a bunch of people come in you don't dare to touch.

steps.name: Anna's Friend
steps.text: This is Grypherburg, after all.

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Ursine Police
steps.text: ...Give your father my regards. I'd appreciate it even more if you gave him my name and number.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: The cop just walked away without saying another thing! I should've slapped him harder.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: That's incredible, Sergo.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But you were telling me that the books revealed that it was the House of Treplev that was supporting the magistrate behind the scenes, and planning to send reinforcements?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Yes. Anna and Natalya talked for a long time last night about your family and friends, especially your father.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: How do they know my associates?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Anna arranged for a few students to return home and go back to school like nothing happened.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: You know the Assembly has students from practically every school. We talked to friends and teachers of those who were arrested. There are many people who care about them, and so we got a lot of information.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Someone said she's already located the Treplev estate and is planning to lay an ambush for the duke. All hearsay and rumors amongst the students, of course—

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Olga... I know this isn't fair to you.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I see no option other than to accept.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'm trapped here with no way to stop whatever they're trying to do. I can only hope for the best.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: I'm glad you see things that way. I'll let you get your rest.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Say, you said you were going to sew a flag for the Assembly and wanted me to collect various kinds of fabric. Have you finished it?

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: I'm sure Anna would want to come and talk to you, if I showed her the flag you made.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'll tell you when I'm done.

steps.name: Sergo
steps.text: Sure! Good night, Olga.
Olga exhales as the door closes silently.

She takes out a long rope tied together from fabric of many different colors, and ties one end to the heavy bed frame made of solid wood. She tugs on it a few times, making sure that it can bear her weight.
Then she goes over to the window and throws the other end out. The rope is immediately swallowed up by the night, as though it has fallen into a bottomless abyss.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I'm sorry, Sergo. I hope Anna won't be too hard on you.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...I won't be making your flag.

a.text: I didn't dare to go home after escaping the theater. I didn't dare to face my father, though he was sure to forgive everything, and I was afraid of the rumored ambush.
I went back to school, looking for someone I could rely on. Professor Valeriya took me in—out of respect for the House of Treplev.
I spent the longest winter night in the professor's dormitory.

steps.name: Ursine Professor
steps.text: ...You must be mistaken.
I understand your wish to protect your students, Professor Valeriya.
However, Olga is not the only student at this school. We need her to help the students who are being held captive.
Please—
The faint silhouette outside the winter suddenly turns its head. Its gaze seems to pierce the thick frosted glass, immediately driving the sleepiness from Olga's head.

She leaps from the bed, not even having the time to put on her shoes, and runs through the back door up the stairs. In her terror, she dares not turn around, even as the footsteps and shouting behind her grow louder.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: *Pant*—*Pant*—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: S-Stay away!

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I should have known. Sergo is gentle-hearted, but prone to naivete. He was always likely to make a mistake.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: There is still time to rectify the mistake, however.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: How did you find me? Do you even have spies in our school?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: These past few days, I combed every school in Grypherburg for potential allies, following the list of missing students.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You sought sanctuary at your school as soon as you escaped the theater... you're exactly who I think you are.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Where else could I go? Sergo told me you have assassins hiding around my home.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Is it true that you're trying to kill my father?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I have neither the intention nor the ability to deal with the Ursine aristocracy that way. We have always operated by negotiation.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I believed you when you promised to rescue the students that night, because I felt guilty about what happened to them.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But what did you do to me? Tricked me and locked me up in a room! Did you think I'd still trust you?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I don't know where you heard these rumors—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Stay away from me!
Olga stumbles back a few steps, leaning against the windowsill at the end of the stairway, her hands pressed against the window frame.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I've had enough, Anna!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I-I don't want my father to be purged because of me, but I can't just watch my fellow students die either.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I just want all this to end! If you'll only be satisfied by making me—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Calm down! Think this through. If anything happens to you, it would be a catastrophe for both your father and the students!

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: The duke would lose his daughter and heir. He would stop at nothing for revenge, to crush us, and everyone in the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: No, no, I just—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I don't know what to do!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Oh—
The cold wind tears at Olga's shawl, threatening to devour her. Suddenly, her arms lose their strength, and she loses her balance, falling backwards out of the window.

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: Olga—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...I was lucky to fall right into the middle of the pile. I escaped from Morozova with only minor injuries.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I hid in the city for a day, until my father's men found me and took me home.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: That is the extent of my account.
The chamber is once again filled with chatter, though a single sigh stands out, as though a tremendous weight has been lifted off one pair of shoulders.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Baryshnya Trepleva, from your point of view, how did the students enter the Treplev estate?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I don't know how they did it, but given that Anna already knew where it was, they would have had their pick of options.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Well... I'm sure the entire committee has arrived at an answer.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Still, I must follow protocol and confirm this—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Baryshnya Trepleva, do you accuse Anna Morozova, leader of the Student Assembly, of colluding with Sonya Mykhailivna, and committing various crimes, including treason?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I accuse the leader of the Student Assembly...

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Olga Danilovna Trepleva, of responsibility for all acts involving the students in the Katorga Incident.

steps.name: Duke Treplev
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Anna Morozova should be penalized for blackmailing the nobility, but she only did what she did out of urgent necessity—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Do you know what you are saying, Baryshnya Trepleva?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I am stating the truth, Your Honor.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Ever since Zoya took the stand, everyone in the room knew the source of the storm, yet no one was willing to say her name.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: Who was the leader and organizer of the Student Assembly, who pushed it down this path, who is responsible for this broken order...

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I declare that I shall willingly don the shackles I deserve—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Recess! Recess!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Stop writing, parliamentarian! Escort Baryshnya Trepleva out for fresh air, now!
The testimony once again sets the hearing on fire. The roaring of the duke and the animated discussions quickly drown out the feeble hammering of the gavel.
Olga lowers her gaze as she is escorted out by the parliamentarian, past Absinthe on the witness stand.
Absinthe nods slightly.
Hah—hah——
Get, up, here!

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I'm not letting go! Stay put!
Istina is leaning out the window, both hands locked around Olga's arms, hanging on with all her might.
The others rush forward to pull Istina and Olga back into the hallway in a chorus of heave-hos and panting.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Hah—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You can't die here, Olga. Didn't you hear what I said?

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: But, I could never be, as ruthless as you are—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Ruthless?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Tell me, were you really planning to jump when you were sitting on that windowsill?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Your problem was never that you couldn't be ruthless. You were simply running away.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: When you decided to hold the protest, and now... you were fearless in opposing everything, simply because you knew—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: No matter what you did, all you needed to do was to turn around, and you would find yourself in your father's embrace.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You never knew what it felt like to struggle to survive, you never even imagined it. You simply dreamed one day after another, in the cradle that your family has woven for you...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Do you think all the other people in the land of Ursus get to dream the same dream?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Let me tell you this, Olga.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You have never truly seen your country, seen Ursus for what it is. Innocence is a sin in this land, and indecision its greatest accomplice, but you have continued to avoid choosing your path.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: If you wanted to continue to dream, you should have gone back to your father a long time ago, and sat by the warm fireside watching the executioner's axe fall on our futures.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: If you want to rescue the students, you need to put all your chips on the table, even your own family.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I have already made my choice... stand up, Olga.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I'm taking you back, whether you like it or not. I will show you how we get the others out of the quarantine zone.

steps.name: Anxious Student
steps.text: We have to go, Anna. We've already caused quite the commotion on campus. The students helping us can only delay them for so long.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: ...Let's go back to the theater.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Students can't remain students forever, Olga. Everyone has something that they must do... and what I must do now is make you disappear for a while.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You will be freed once the situation has been resolved.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...One moment, Anna.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: You know where the Treplev estate is...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Yes, but I have no intention of killing your father. I only want to convince him.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: To save the students?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: ...I have an idea.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: There is a secret passage that leads to the manor's wine cellar, accessible through the warehouse of a vineyard on the western outskirts of Grypherburg.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: It is my father's escape route in the event of an assassination attempt... not even the guards know about it. You can enter the manor through there, and he will know at once that it was I who told you about it.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Olga...

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: You understand that this will ruin your relationship with your family beyond repair.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: No, Anna.

steps.name: Olga
steps.text: I will defend my honor and that of my house, in my own way.
